blocks.text: The defenders insist that this is the hour to fight and die, not to beg or retreat, and the battle inside the fort becomes close, confused, and merciless.
Weapons, bodies, and men crash together at gates and breaches until even kin and comrades are hard to distinguish in the smoke and pressure.
The page frames the siege not as orderly warfare but as a final moral trial in which shame matters more than survival.
